newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges business leaders to aid welfare plan.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges business leaders to aid welfare plan.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton asked business leaders on Friday to help move people from welfare to work, saying that a new welfare reform law "cannot succeed by government action alone."

At a White House meeting with top corporate executives, Clinton also said that the budget he will submit in February will provide incentives "attractive to the private sector" to encourage the hiring of welfare recipients.

"Unless we can create new jobs in the private sector within the two-year time frame, the welfare reform effort will not succeed," Clinton said, referring to a provision of the new law which gives people on public assistance two years to find work or face a cut-off of benefits.

"Our budget plan has provisions in it to support the business community in helping to create a million more jobs," the president added, referring to tax incentives and other measures that he talked about in his re-election campaign.
Clinton met with the business leaders shortly after the government said in its latest unemployment report that 11.2 million new jobs had been created over the last four years.

He said the unprecedented job growth showed the strength of the economy and the effectiveness of the administration's economic strategy, and added that he was confident it would not rekindle inflationary pressure in the economy.
